arms.note: *jumping=true every frame -> held -> 0 jumps, spins on ground
jump toggled on ground contact + air-strafe gated to airborne

finding: Holding +jump every frame jumps once then holds, so the bot never bunnyhops (0 jumps/min, 0% airborne, spins on the ground at ~138 qu/s). Toggling the jump on ground contact (press on landing, release in air) plus gating the velocity-aware air-strafe to airborne takes a from-scratch accelerator to 80 jumps/min, 96% airborne, max 476 qu/s on trick.bsp. Acceleration is real but not yet sustained (median 75) and still far from the human benchmark (880/1088): tuning (numerator sweep) and strafe refinement are the next step. The held-jump bug likely also crippled the unconditional-jump moveprobe modes (5-9, 11), a candidate explanation for the chronic weak bot air-speed (S7: 122 vs 433).
spawn: Frogbots only spawn on map_supported maps (a bots/maps/<map>.bot must load). trick.bsp ships none. scripts/generate_bot_route.py builds one programmatically from a demo trajectory (trick5.cmds -> 180 walkable markers); no in-game waypoint editor needed. The bot is driven by moveprobe, so the route graph need not be navigable.
